newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report. [CORRECTED 01:00 GMT 10/7]
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report. [CORRECTED 01:00 GMT 10/7]

text.p: The South African rand was charting new five-month lows toward's Wednesday's close following a surge in offshore interest in the dollar.
The local unit was last priced at 4.5600/5630 rand to the dollar from 4.5500/5530 late Tuesday.
The offshore demand saw the unit break key resistance at 4.56 but dealers said the Reserve Bank was trying to muffle the move by selling dollars.
"There just a lot of offshore demand all of a sudden. The central bank's in and he's being hit everywhere," said a frantic Johannesburg forex dealer.
The rand's weakness coincided with the dollar hitting a fresh 41-month peak against the mark of 1.7650.
The local unit has been dogged by offshore nervousness about emerging market currencies and the effect continued gold price falls might have on the South African economy.
Market sentiment was also dented by an overnight DRI/McGraw-Hill report ranking South Africa as having the highest investment risk among world's 10 largest emerging markets.
In cross rate trading, the rand was last at 0.3856/3859 marks from 0.3860/3864 marks on Tuesday and 24.7179/7451 yen from 24.6944/7326 before.
Against sterling the rand stood at 7.6835/6936 from 7.6931/7028 on Tuesday.

The Reserve Bank earlier told Reuters it was not engineering a fall in the rand on the back of recent falls in the gold price, despite market talk it had been buying dollars (corrects from "selling dollars") to get the rand to more exporter and reserve-friendly levels
The late afternoon saw South African gilts back at their intraday worst as profit-taking and rand jitters took their toll in a relatively thin market.
"The rand's just not looking healthy and that (DRI/McGraw Hill) emerging report has left us smarting a bit too," said one bond dealer.
At 1402 GMT, the benchmark R150 bond was quoted at 14.235 percent bid from Tuesday's 1507 GMT level of 14.10 percent.
The R150 earlier failed to sustain a break below resistance at 14.18 percent.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged between 15.25 and 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said Tuesday's money market shortage fell to 6.099 billion rand from Monday's adjusted total of 6.284 billion rand.
Foreigners were net buyers of 270.295 million rand's worth of bonds on Tuesday after buying 344.25 million rand's worth on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
